Question: Did the decision on assignment of judgment enforcement decision to the executor to organize the execution of judgment execution decision?
Law Context: Article 36 of the Law on Civil Judgment Enforcement stipulates that heads of civil judgment enforcement agencies shall proactively issue enforcement decisions on the following parts of judgments and decisions: a) Fine, retrospective collection of illicitly earned money and assets and court fees; b) return of money and asset to involved parties; c) Confiscation into state funds, confiscation for destruction of material evidence and assets; d) Recovery of land use rights and other assets to be remitted into state fund; e) Decision on application of provisional urgent measures. Within 5 working days after receiving a judgment or ruling, the head of the civil judgment enforcement agency shall issue a judgment enforcement decision. Within 24 hours after receiving a decision on application of provisional urgent measures, which is transferred by the court or directly handed to the involved party, the head of the civil judgment enforcement agency shall issue a judgment enforcement decision and assign an enforcer to organize the enforcement. Apart from the cases mentioned above, the head of the civil judgment enforcement authority shall only issue a judgment enforcement decision when a written request for judgment enforcement is made. The time limit for issuing a judgment enforcement decision is 5 working days after receiving a written request for judgment enforcement. Within 2 working days after issuing a judgment enforcement decision, the head of the civil judgment enforcement agency shall assign an enforcer to organize the execution of such decision. Article 2 of the Circular No. 22/2011/TT-BTP dated December 02,2001 of the Ministry of Justice providing guidance on administrative management of civil judgment enforcement stipulates that the judgment enforcement decision is the basis for the enforcement officer to prepare the judgment execution dossier. Within 2 working days after being assigned, the enforcer shall compile a judgment execution dossier. The judgment enforcement dossier must show the entire process of judgment enforcement by the enforcement officer. The enforcement officer shall record the work and retain all documents that have been and are being executed in the judgment enforcement dossier, including the judgment; the record on handover and handling of exhibits and property distrained or impounded; the verification record, the record of judgment enforcement (with signatures of the litigants on all pages); the notice, summons, invitation, requests, complaints, receipts, receipts and payment notes, documents related to the handling of property serving judgment enforcement, official dispatches and papers of the enforcement agency, relevant organizations and individuals, such as: official dispatchers of instructions on judgment enforcement; Currently, there is no legal document providing that the assignment of executors to organize the execution of judgment enforcement decisions by decisions is to limit troublesome administrative procedures in civil judgment enforcement activities.

Question: Is the child in artificial insemination, does the husband have to support when he gets divorced?
Law Context: Juror Vu Thi Nhung - Everest Law Company - responded: We cite some provisions of the 2014 Marriage and Family Law for your reference, as follows: "Birth with assisted reproductive technology is the birth of a child by artificial insemination or in vitro fertilization" (Clause 21 Article 3). Identification of parents in case of giving birth with assisted reproductive technology: "In case the wife gives birth with the assisted reproductive technique, the identification of parents shall comply with the provisions of Article 88 of this Law" (Clause 1 of Article 92). "Identify parent:" 1 - Children born during the marriage period or conceived by the wife during the marital period are common children of husband and wife. Children born within 300 days after the marriage termination shall be considered children conceived by the wife during the marriage period. Children born before the date of marriage registration and recognized by their parents as common children of husband and wife. 2. In cases where the parents do not recognize the children, there must be evidences and such must be determined by the Court " (Article 88). Obligations and rights of parents who do not directly raise children after divorce: "Fathers and mothers who don't directly raise their children have the obligation to support their children" (Clause 2 of Article 82). Pursuant to the above provisions of law, a child of the couple is born by assisted reproductive technology and is born during the marriage period, therefore, the child is still identified as the common child of both of them. In case of divorce, if husband or sister does not directly raise the child, he/she must provide nursing care for the child as prescribed in Clause 2 Article 82 of the Law on marriage and family 2014.

Question: Does a corporation require a Control Board?
Law Context: A joint-stock company is a company whose charter capital is divided into multiple equal parts called shares according to the Law on Enterprises 2014. A joint-stock company has at least 03 shareholders that may be organizations or individuals, and the maximum number of shareholders is unlimited. A joint-stock company has the legal person status from the date of issuance of its enterprise registration certificate. Joint-stock companies may issue shares of various types to raise capital. Pursuant to Article 134 of the Law on Enterprises 2014, a joint-stock company may choose to organize management and operate according to one of the two following models, unless otherwise prescribed by securities laws: - General meeting of shareholders, Board of Directors, Control Board, and Director/General Director. In case a joint-stock company has fewer than 11 shareholders and institutional shareholders own less than 50% of the company's total shares, the Control Board (referred to as model 1) is not required. - General shareholders' meeting, Board of directors and Director or General Director. In this case, at least 20% of the members of the Board of Directors must be independent members and there must be an internal audit board affiliated to the Board. Independent members perform the function of supervising and organizing the control over the management and administration of the company (called model 2). - In case the company has 11 shareholders or more: the Control Board must be established; - In cases the company's shareholders are organizations owning 50% or more of the company'total shares: the Controllers' Committee must be set up; - Where the company owns less than 11 shareholder or more and shareholders are organization owning less than 50 %, the Control Committee is not required to be setup. The establishment of the Control Board is based on the needs of the company. For model 2: The model of Shareholder general assembly, Board of Directors and Director/General Director. If the joint-stock company selects the management and operation of the company according to this model, the Control Board is not required to be established. However, the Board of directors of the company must have at least 20% of its members being independent members and the company shall have an internal audit department affiliated to the Board. In this case, independent members perform the function of supervising and organizing the control over the management and administration of the company. Follow the above instructions. The above is our perspective on the matter you are asking. Thank you!

Law Context: He Thien, who discovered the ancient bronze urn buried in his own land, did not want to give it up to the competent authorities. In this case, the following issues should be considered: the legal regime for the property dug by Thien's family; the responsibility of the commune People's Committee when the village chief reports it; the establishment of ownership over the old bronze lamp and the interests of Thien when discovering that old bronze one. Article 187 of the 2005 Civil Code provides for the right to possess property which is dropped, mislaid, buried, sunk or of which the owner is unidentifiable, and Article 240 of the Civil Code 2015 provides for and establishes ownership rights with respect to buried or sunk objects found. At the same time, it is necessary to apply the provisions of the 2001 Cultural Heritage Law and the Government's Decree No. 92/2002/ND-CP of November 11,2012 detailing the implementation of a number of articles of the Cultural Heritage Laws. - Legal regime for the property dug up by the Thien family: Clause 1, Article 187 of the 2005 Civil Code stipulates that the person who discovers the dropped, mislaid, buried or sunk property must immediately notify or return it to the owner; if the owner is not known, he/she must notify or hand it over to the People's Committee of the commune, ward or township or the nearest grassroots police or other competent state agencies as prescribed by law. According to the provisions of Clause 4, Article 14 of the 2001 Cultural Heritage Law, organizations and individuals are obliged to promptly notify places where vestiges, antiques, national precious objects, historical-cultural relics or scenic places are discovered; and hand over vestigues, antiquities and national precious things they have found to the nearest competent state agencies. Based on the above provisions, Thien shall promptly notify and hand over the antique copper stove to the commune People's Committee or police office. Within the period from the time of discovery of the bronze jar to the time it is handed over to a competent state agency, Thien shall preserve such bronze jar. - Regarding the responsibility of the commune People's Committees when being informed of the discovery of the bronze idol by Thien According to Article 51 of the Government's Decree No. 92/2002/ND-CP of November 11,2012, detailing the implementation of a number of articles of the Cultural Heritage Law, the communes' People' s Committees shall have to : To fulfill their responsibilities, the commune People's Committee should send officials to meet Thien directly to explain and mobilize him to voluntarily hand over the copper torch to the cultural agency for appraisal. The handover must be recorded in writing. The contents of the record should clearly state the full name and address of Mr. Thien; the full names and positions of the receiver; the time and place where Mr. T.found the bronze lamp; characteristics and conditions of the bronze flame when it is handed over by Mr.Ts. - The establishment of ownership over the ancient bronze jar and Mr Thien's interests When the cultural agency has appraised and as provided for in Article 240 of the 2005 Civil Code, the bronze jar is an antique and should belong to the State. Mr. Thien is entitled to a reward amount as prescribed by law. The reward levels are specified in Article 53 of Decree No. 92/2002/ND-CP.

Question: Is the land in the relics area granted land use right certificate?
Law Context: 1. Article 101 of the 2013 Law on Land provides for: 1 Households and individuals that are using land before the effective date of this Law without the papers specified in Article 100 of this law and have permanent residence registration in localities and are directly engaged in agricultural production, forestry, aquaculture or salt making in areas with difficult or exceptionally difficult socio-economic conditions, and are certified by commune-level People's Committees of localities where exists the land as having stably and dispute-free land use rights, shall be granted certificates of land use right and ownership of houses and other land-attached assets without having to pay land use levy. 2. Households and individuals currently using land without the papers specified in Article 100 of this Law but the land has been stably used since before July 1,2004, and does not violate the land law, and now certified by commune-level People's Committees as dispute-free and conformable with land use master plans, detailed urban construction master plans and master plans on construction of rural residential areas approved by competent state agencies, for areas with master plans. They will be granted certificates of land use rights and ownership of houses and other land-attached assets. According to the above provisions, one of the conditions for grant of land use right certificates for land which has been used stably and long term without papers is that such land was used stately before July 1,2004, does not violate the land law, is certified by commune-level People's Committees as dispute-free and conformable with land use plannings, detailed urban construction plannings or plannings on construction of rural residential areas already approved by competent state agencies. On the other hand, according to the provisions of the 2013 Land Law, land with classified historical-cultural relics or scenic places must be strictly protected. In special cases where it is necessary to use land with historical-culture relic or scenic place for non-business purposes, such use must comply with the approved land use master plans and plans and obtain written approval of state agencies competent to decide on relic ranking. Refer to the abovementioned provisions in the case of you and your family using a land parcel of 103 m2 since 1989, which has been fully paid tax annually, the receipt is still valid, and you wish to register the land use right but the commune cadastral officer considers that the land is trespassed on and belongs to the relics. In this case, your family should look at the cadastral map of the commune: If the land is in a historical-cultural site, then your family is not eligible to be granted a land use right certificate. If you are not in a historic or cultural site as the cadastral officer informed your family, and it is in line with the land use planning, detailed urban construction planning, or rural residential planning approved by the competent authority, and does not violate the land law, and the land is certified by the People's Committee as dispute-free, you may be issued with a certificate of land use rights. The above is the advisory of the Editorial Board of the Law Secretary on the grant of land use right certificates for land lying in relics. You should consult the 2013 Land Law to understand the law. " Whoever mobilizes or assigns persons who do not have driving licenses or licenses or who don't fully satisfy the conditions prescribed by law to operate road vehicles, causing loss of lives or serious damage to the health and/or property of other persons, shall be imposed a fine of between three million dong and thirty million dong, subject to non-custodial reform of up to three years or a prison term of between one and three years. Question: Does singing in the festival do the agency have to pay for copyright?
Law Context: If the song's author has been dead for 50 years or more, the song is considered a work of public interest. This gives any organization or individual the right to use the copyright without paying royalties to the authors. If not falling into the above case, according to Clause 1, Article 25 of the 2005 Intellectual Property Law, when performing a song at cultural activities and propagation events free of charge in any form, the copyright royalty paid to the author is not required. The cases in which royalties must be paid to musicians In accordance with Clause 3 of article 20 and Clause 1 of article 36 of the Law on Intellectual Property, any individual or organization exploiting or using a song which is not a work belonging to the public, must pay royalties to the author if it collects money in any form (including receipt of advertising or sponsorship, etc.). According to Clause 1 of Article 25, when you make copies for scientific research, reasonably cite a work for comment, illustration or teaching, duplicate a work to be kept in a library, etc., you are not required to pay royalties, remuneration or copyright to the author. In general, non-profit and public service activities that use a work for community or research purposes do not require the authors to pay royalties. How much royalties would it cost to the musician to copyright the musician? Essentially, the royalties or copyrights for the use or exploitation of a song are paid on the basis of an agreement between the song user and the song's author. For songs owned by the State or created, exploited or used by organizations and individuals with state budget funds, the payment level shall be calculated according to the royalty bracket, remuneration bracket or a percentage of the performance turnover specified in Decree No. 21/2015/ND-CP.

Question: Is the land use right certificate to a child considered a testament?
Law Context: Pursuant to Point dd Clause 3 Article 140 of the 2015 Civil Code, the authorized representative shall terminate in the following cases: - The principal or the authorized person dies; the principal or authorized person is no longer a juridical person. This way, when your father dies, the power of attorney will no longer be valid. Your brother will have to terminate the land use as per his signed authorization. In regard to whether or not this power of attorney can be considered a will, we would like to reply as follows: Pursuant to Article 624 of the 2015 Civil Code: - A will is the expression of the will of an individual to transfer his/her property to another person after his/ her death. - The testator must be sound and clear-headed during the test preparation; must not be deceived, threatened or coerced; - The contents of the will must not violate the prohibitions of the law and social ethics; the form of the testament must not contravene the law. In your case, your father only issued a land use right certificate to your sister, not specifically the transfer of land use rights to your brother after his death. Furthermore, the paper was no longer valid, the authorization work was terminated.

In case an arbitration agreement is established by an incompetent person but the person competent to establish such agreement accepts or knows about it during the process of establishment and performance of the arbitration agreement or in arbitral proceedings without objection, the arbitration contract is not invalid. Law Context: Application for recording in civil status register of marriage of Vietnamese citizens which has been processed by competent foreign authorities includes documents specified under Subsection 9 Section I Part II of Decision 299/QD-BTP dated 2016 on new administrative procedures in civil registration implemented by domestic civil registration agencies under management of Ministry of Justice, to be specific: * Papers to be presented - Passports or ID cards or Citizen Identity Cards or other valid documents with photo and personal information issued by competent agencies to prove personal identity of persons requesting marriage note (identity papers); - Papers proving place of residence to determine authority If the application is sent by post, certified true copies of the above-mentioned documents must be enclosed. - Copy of marriage certificate issued by foreign competent authorities; - Copy personal identification papers of both male and female partners, if the dossier is sent by post; - If a Vietnamese citizen has divorced or annulled his/her marriage at a foreign competent authority, an extract of the recording of the divorce or annulment in the civil status book (the extract of divorce note) must be submitted. - A letter of authorization as prescribed by law in case of authorization for marriage note. In case the authorized person is the grandparent, parent, child, spouse or sibling of the authorizing person, the power of attorney is not required to be notarized or certified but must contain papers proving the relationship with the authorizer. The above is the reply about the papers and documents in the dossier for recording in the civil status book the marriage of a Vietnamese citizen which has been settled at a competent foreign agency. For a better understanding and more detailed discussion of this issue, read and refer to the 2016 Decision No. 299/QD-BTP for more information. Thank you!

Question: Can you reapply back the papers filed in court?
Law Context: The current procedural law does not provide for the return of evidence (being original papers) to involved parties after trial. Because the original papers have been included in the case file and are considered evidence for the settlement of the case, the Court has no basis to resolve the request for re-issuance of these papers. However, as prescribed in Article 91 of the 2015 Code of Civil Procedure, during the process of the court's resolution of a civil case, involved parties have the right and obligation to hand over evidence to the court; if involved parties fail to hand in or fully hand in evidence, they shall bear the consequences of their failure to hand or fully do so, unless otherwise provided by law. The handover of evidences by involved parties to courts must be recorded in writing. The minutes must clearly state the name, form, content and characteristics of evidence; number of copies and pages of evidence and time of receipt; signatures or fingerprints of the deliverer and recipient and the court's seal. The record must be made in two copies, one to be filed in the civil case file and the other to be kept by the involved party who has submitted evidence. In accordance with the above provisions, if you request the Supreme People's Court to review the case according to cassation procedures, your family may present evidence to protect their legitimate rights and interests. If the evidence has been submitted to the court, the evidence submission record will be presented to prove it. When reviewing a case according to cassation procedures, the Supreme People's Court shall study the entire case file forwarded by the appellate court. The evidence your family has filed in the case file will be reviewed by the Supreme People's Court. The above is the Editorial Board of the Law Clerk's advice on re-applying papers filed in court. Refer to the 2015 Civil Procedure Code for details on how to read this section. Thank you!
